newsitem.title: ZAIRE: More foreigners evacuated from eastern Zaire.
newsitem.headline: More foreigners evacuated from eastern Zaire.

text.p: More foreigners, including aid workers and civilians, were evacuated from eastern Zaire on Sunday as further fighting between Rwandan rebels and Zaire government troops was reported.
Bukavu was tense as the sound of distant cannon fire from the south echoed round the town, and Zairean troops, recently reinforced, were noticeably nervous.
A 27-seater plane evacuated French and Italian nationals from Bukavu, including diplomats, aid workers and civilians, without incident.
On Saturday the United Nations sent two planes to Bukavu to evacuate 128 U.N. and other foreign workers after conflict between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops threatened to engulf the region.

U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali had earlier called for an emergency mission to go to Zaire, followed by an international conference to prevent warfare spreading throughout the Central African region.

North of Lake Kivu at Goma, where fighting had been reported around a string of refugee camps along the Zaire-Rwanda border, 22 non-essential aid workers were flown out in a U.N. aircraft, bound for Nairobi.
World Food Programme (WFP) spokeswoman Brenda Barton in Nairobi said there were still about 100 international aid workers in the Goma area, with no immediate plans for a complete evacuation.
"The situation is tense but not critical. We are watching developments closely," she added.
Aid officials in Goma said there were reports of small-arms fire at two refugee camps north of the town, but it was not clear what had happened.

The rebels have captured several towns and have panicked hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees into fleeing their camps, creating a major humanitarian problem in an area where aid facilities were already stretched.
